weakness.description: Git-push prohibitions extracted from combined user turns include broad exec bindings and command-pattern ambiguity, causing Claude Code to block non-push actions such as git status and file reads.

The extractor collapses multiple behavioral clauses into one contract: a prohibition plus risk-first reporting preference is stored as one prohibition, and a four-rule e2e turn becomes one path-scoped contract so git push and web search are allowed out of scope.

Web-search and external-message restrictions are not bound to adapter-native actions reliably: Codex web-search rules lack web.search constraints, and Nanobot send_message raises ActionSignature validation instead of producing a gate decision.

Natural phrases such as 'in the workspace' and 'do not touch generated manifests' normalize to bad or missing scope/action bindings, creating either irrelevant path scopes like 'the' or unbound project-wide prohibitions that overblock local reads and doc edits.

Command-specific prohibitions such as git push still become ambiguous blockers for unrelated direct actions. In Phase 1, the e2e local file.write probe was blocked by the git-push contract even though the signature host_action was file.write, not git.push.

The extractor stores clauses such as 'do not publish anything yet' as prohibitions with no host_actions or canonical_tags, so ActionGate treats ordinary read-only shell probes as ambiguous violations instead of binding the rule to publish/external-write actions only.

Prompt intake omits repo-scoped action restrictions when no file or component target is present, even when the new user turn explicitly asks to browse/check online. The Codex web-search rule is stored and gated, but render_prompt_context returns empty for a web-search-shaped prompt.

improvement: Split compound user turns into separate durable contracts while preserving leading repo/session/task scope.
Removed broad exec predicate binding when a more specific action such as git.push, git.commit, or dependency.install is available.
Added extraction, compiler, signature, and adapter coverage for web.search, message.send, email.send, and memory.write actions.
Prevented phrases like in the workspace from becoming path scope and inferred generated/** for generated artifact edit/touch rules.
Verified with PYTHONPATH=src UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run pytest: 57 passed.
Set runner_path to include PYTHONPATH=src so the reusable Critic runner imports current working-tree source under uv --no-editable.

weakness.description: When a later broader clause such as "do not publish anything yet" or "do not browse for package docs" overlaps an earlier explicit action rule, ConflictResolver records it as a refinement edge and ActionGate reports the broader clause as the enforcing contract. The action is blocked, but the prompt/gate explanation loses the more precise user-approved boundary such as git push without approval or web search without asking, weakening auditability and user-facing recovery guidance.

improvement: Changed command-pattern evaluation so git-push predicates do not ambiguously match direct non-shell actions such as file.write.
Bound generic publish prohibitions to git.push plus external_write/publish_code tags instead of leaving them as unbound ambiguous blockers.
Added prompt-intake action hints so repo/project rules surface when a user turn asks to browse, publish, edit, or notify even without path targets.
Added focused regression tests for direct-action non-overblocking, publish clause binding, and action-hint prompt retrieval.
Verified with PYTHONPATH=src UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run pytest: 59 passed.

weakness.description: A user turn that combines task work with a bare-file restriction, "Update package.json ... but do not edit package-lock.json", is stored as a project-scoped file-write prohibition with no path_globs. MAC correctly blocks package-lock.json edits, but also blocks package.json edits that the user explicitly requested, because ScopeNormalizer and PolicyCompiler do not bind bare filename targets into path scope or target predicates.

improvement: Restricted deterministic refinement classification so broader same-action clauses are independent unless they are actually narrower or clarifying.
Preserved specific approval-boundary contracts when later broader publish/browse clauses overlap the same action.
Ranked gate evaluation by binding and scope specificity so the block reason favors the more actionable specific rule.
Added regression tests for broader publish-clause independence and specific approval-boundary gate explanations.
Verified with PYTHONPATH=src UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run pytest: 61 passed.

weakness.description: A mixed Codex task turn such as "Update package.json ... but do not edit package-lock.json" still binds the prohibition to the positive task target package.json rather than the negated target package-lock.json. Prompt intake returns no lockfile reminder, ActionGate allows package-lock.json writes as out_of_scope, and blocks the requested package.json edit.

improvement: Added bare filename path-scope extraction for explicit file targets such as package-lock.json.
Added bare filename target predicate compilation so file.write rules match only the named file target.
Added regressions for bare filename scope normalization and package-lock.json vs package.json predicate matching.
Verified with PYTHONPATH=src UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run pytest: 63 passed.

weakness.description: Mixed current-task turns with slash-qualified file restrictions such as "do not edit docs/archive.md" are extracted as path-scoped prohibitions, but ScopeNormalizer/PolicyCompiler select only the basename archive.md. Prompt intake omits the rule for docs/archive.md and ActionGate allows the forbidden docs/archive.md edit as out_of_scope.

Category restrictions such as "do not modify lockfiles" are stored as project-scoped file-write prohibitions with no target predicate. MAC correctly blocks package-lock.json, but also blocks the explicitly requested package.json edit because lockfile category language is not normalized to a narrow target class.

improvement: Split mixed current-task turns so the durable negated clause is extracted independently from the positive task instruction.
Selected bare filename targets after negation triggers such as do not, never, and must not so package-lock.json is preferred over the requested package.json edit.
Applied the same negated bare filename target selection in scope normalization and policy compilation.
Fixed the clause splitter indentation so raw_parts is initialized whether or not a leading repo/project prefix is present.
Added regression coverage for mixed task turns that prohibit package-lock.json while allowing package.json.
Verified with PYTHONPATH=src UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run pytest: 65 passed.
